clue.text: Tree that has flourished to help the cameraman

parts.note: fl. is the abbreviation for floruit, Latin for 'flourished', used before a person's active dates
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A tree that has thrived is pressed into service by a photographer, perhaps as a backdrop.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is named first but its letters come last: FL + ASH gives FLASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographer uses a sudden burst of bright light from a lamp to illuminate a dim scene.

clue.text: If painter is philosopher, then old money is meat

parts.note: the franc was French currency before the euro
taken as written
bacon is cured pork

explanation.surface: A mock syllogism: if one thing equals another, then money must equal meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Two famous men share the name: the Elizabethan philosopher-statesman and the twentieth-century Irish-born painter. Each half of the clue's 'if... then' defines or builds the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon the philosopher wrote the Novum Organum; his namesake was a celebrated modern painter of distorted figures.

clue.text: Journalist comes in, no less morose of course

indicators.note: something that comes in enters the middle of the other words' letters

parts.note: 'no less morose' means 'as surly', run together
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A gloomy reporter turns up, of course in no better a mood than anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no less morose' has to be rephrased before it gives letters: equally morose is 'as surly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuredly and 'of course' are both adverbs of certainty, used to agree emphatically with a statement.

clue.text: Exalted line of people recited poem

indicators.note: words that are recited are spoken, so the letters are what the ear hears

parts.note: exalted means raised high
a queue is a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: A lofty row of people chanting verse in unison.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'high queue' matches the Japanese verse form.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese verse form of three lines, typically of five, seven and five syllables.

clue.text: See 20
See 20
Musical work for piano in part of 10

indicators.note: one letter placed in the other letters sits inside them

parts.note: 10 is the answer to 10 across; its middle chunk is taken
p is the musical marking for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A piece written for piano that forms a section of some larger work.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue points across the grid: 10 across is CAROUSEL, and only a middle section of it is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for 'work', and composers' pieces are numbered as opuses in catalogues of their output.

clue.text: Barbarian doctor botched the D & C

indicators.note: a botched job is messed up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the Huns were the archetypal barbarian invaders
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A savage surgeon makes a mess of a D & C, a gynaecological scraping procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'D & C' looks like one unit, the surgical procedure, but the D belongs to the anagram and C stands alone as the definition: c. is short for cent, a hundredth of a dollar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cent, abbreviated c, is one hundredth part of a dollar or euro.

clue.text: It's sticky to repeat wrongdoing

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again, as in redo
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Falling back into the same bad habit is a sticky business.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the gummy substance oozing from pine trees and other plants, used in varnish and glue.

clue.text: Promise of success gives a new start to likelihood of doubting, or being doubted

indicators.note: giving something a new start swaps its opening letter for another one

parts.note: taken as written

parts.words: likelihood of doubting, or being doubted
parts.note: suspiciousness is both distrust of others and the quality of looking dubious

explanation.surface: Optimism comes from replacing a habit of doubt, both doubting and being doubted, with something fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'a' is itself the new first letter, ousting the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something auspicious bodes well, so auspiciousness is the quality of signalling good fortune to come.

clue.text: Write to fisherman about way-out Asian stick

indicators.note: letters that are out of place are disordered

parts.note: to pen is to write

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: an angler fishes with rod and line
the letters of this word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A note to an angler about some exotic Asian walking stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way-out' reads as one word meaning eccentric, but it splits into a word and its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Penang lawyer is a walking stick made from a palm stem from Penang in Malaysia, jokingly named as a settler of disputes.

clue.text: Musical to be exciting within classical opening

indicators.note: within means inside, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: the opening two letters of classical
to arouse is to stir up or excite

explanation.surface: A show tune that is thrilling from its very first classical bars.
explanation.walkthrough: C(AROUSE)L: the opening letters of classical wrap around the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Carousel is the 1945 Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show, featuring the song You'll Never Walk Alone.

clue.text: Borderline with benefits

definitions.meaning: first meaning: marginal, on the edge of the mainstream

definitions.note: the answer is the word that goes with benefits
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word that goes with benefits, for perks on top of salary

explanation.surface: Something only just acceptable, but it comes with perks.
explanation.walkthrough: Fringe benefits are extras such as a company car given on top of pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe group or theatre sits on the margins, and fringe benefits are extras beyond wages.

clue.text: Singular bubble with incomplete opening will make one sweat

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining an adjective meaning sweat-inducing

indicators.note: something incomplete is missing a part, here its final letter

parts.note: suds are bubbles of soap, so one bubble is a singular sud
an orifice is an opening in the body

explanation.surface: A lone soap bubble wedged in some partial opening is enough to make anyone break into a sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: Suds is normally only plural, so 'singular bubble' invents a one-bubble form; sudor is Latin for sweat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudorific is a medical term for something that induces perspiration, from Latin sudor, sweat.

clue.text: Horrid quarrel where one's taken for a ride

definitions.text: where one's taken for a ride

parts.note: rotten means nasty or horrid
a row (rhyming with cow) is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A nasty argument at the end of which someone feels conned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken for a ride' suggests being swindled, but Rotten Row is a track in London's Hyde Park for horse riding.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten Row is the bridleway along the south side of Hyde Park, where riders exercise their horses.

clue.text: Little bird with little daughter on my lawn

parts.note: a chick is a young bird
wee is Scottish for small
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A fledgling and a small girl out playing on the setter's grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of where the answer is found: a weed growing in the setter's lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Chickweed is a small, creeping white-flowered plant that commonly invades gardens and grass.

clue.text: President's backing for Thursday budget speech

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the letters are read right to left
the letters sit inside the run of words of this speech

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A US President endorsing the British Chancellor's Thursday budget statement.
explanation.walkthrough: thursDAY BUDget, read backwards, gives the nickname. Budget speeches in Britain have traditionally been delivered by the Chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubya, a Texan drawl of the letter W, was the nickname of George W. Bush, US President 2001 to 2009.

clue.text: Weaver on strike wants to settle at lowest level

parts.note: Nick Bottom is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
striking workers are out

explanation.surface: A textile worker on strike hopes to settle at the minimum pay grade.
explanation.walkthrough: Weaver is capitalised so it reads as a job, but it names Shakespeare's Bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices or an economy bottom out when they reach their lowest point and stop falling.

clue.text: Yeats's work so far

indicators.note: to work something is to shape it, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the poet's name, taken as written

explanation.surface: A reference to the output of the Irish poet W B Yeats to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean up to now, until the present time, as in 'no news yet'.

clue.text: Assembly in Berlin in case right is challenged

indicators.note: being challenged disturbs things, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal ruling in the German parliament is appealed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reichstag building in Berlin houses the Bundestag, Germany's parliament, and was the assembly's historic name.

clue.text: World of the fortunate caught by shore bird

definitions.meaning: first meaning: from the saying that the world is a lucky person's shellfish
second meaning: the prey named in the oystercatcher's name

explanation.surface: Luck and a wading bird hunting on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The world is your oyster' means everything lies open to you; the oystercatcher is a black-and-white shore bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb makes the shellfish stand for the lucky person's world, and a seabird is named after catching it.

clue.text: Dancing dervishes never refer to boss — NB musical

indicators.note: dancers move about, so these letters move around into a new order

parts.words: dervishes never refer to boss — NB
parts.note: every letter of these words is reshuffled

explanation.surface: Whirling dervishes are warned never to consult their leader, a note marked NB.
explanation.walkthrough: All twenty-seven letters, NB included, are the fodder. The grid holds SEVEN only once, in 20 down; it is read twice to make the full title across 20, 4 down and 4 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven Brides for Seven Brothers is a 1954 MGM film musical about backwoods brothers seeking wives.

clue.text: Musical state

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1943 Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show
second meaning: the US state whose capital is its namesake city

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description, a musical state of mind, but it is two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rodgers and Hammerstein show takes its title from the American territory where it is set, later a state.

clue.text: Check on half the listeners

indicators.note: taking half leaves only part, so the tail of the word goes

parts.note: auditors, in an older sense, are hearers or listeners

explanation.surface: Checking on half the audience, perhaps to see if they are paying attention.
explanation.walkthrough: AUDITORS is cut down, keeping the first five of its eight letters; 'half' is generous.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection of accounts, so to audit is to check them.

clue.text: Repetitious Elizabethan writer

parts.note: surface: an Elizabethan author who keeps saying the same thing
setter's reading: the author's surname is a two-letter chunk said twice over

explanation.walkthrough: John Lyly was an Elizabethan author, best known for Euphues; his name is the adverb ending -LY repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: John Lyly was a sixteenth-century English writer and playwright whose ornate prose gave rise to the word euphuism.

clue.text: Strong resistance to placing of shroud for setter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an emphatic refusal, never while I live
second meaning: where a shroud would be laid over the setter's corpse

explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' means the person who wrote the clue, so 'my' is the setter speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the phrase signals absolute opposition, and literally it is where a burial sheet lies on a corpse.

clue.text: Not moved by exhibition of nudes without method

indicators.note: an exhibition shows things off in a fresh display, so the letters are rearranged
without in its old sense means outside, so these letters go around the other piece

parts.note: the letters of this word are rearranged
a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: Someone unimpressed by a gallery show of naked figures that lacks any technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means outside: UNS(WAY)ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unswayed means not influenced or persuaded, keeping one's position unchanged.

clue.text: Instructor who's lost in Student Representative Council

definitions.text: Instructor who's lost in Student Representative Council

parts.words: Instructor who's lost in Student Representative Council
parts.note: surface: a teacher bewildered at a meeting of the student union
setter's reading: a university teacher, out of place among elected student delegates

explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay, if any, is obscure; the clue works as a description of a university teacher with no role on a student-run body.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a university teacher who guides small groups of students, as distinct from their elected representatives.
